title: रञ्जना लिपिया म्हबो
nepali: भारतय्‌ बोलंगु ब्राम्ही लिपिया विकासक्रमय्‌ नेपालय्‌ थःगु हे पहः दुगु नेपाल लिपिया विकास जुल । ब्राम्ही लिपिया कालावधि सामान्यतः ईपूया निगू शताब्दीनिसें ईशाया प्यंगूगु शताब्दीतक माने यानातःगु दु । थुकिया दथुइ थो आखः रूपय्‌ छुं हिउपाः वःगु लूगु दु । थुगु हिउपालं ईशाया सोंगूगु शदी छगू न्हूगु रूप बोलनावल । थुकियात गुप्त लिपिया नां बियाबिल, छाय्‌कि भारतया गुप्त सम्राट पिनिगु कालय्‌ न्हापाया ब्राम्हीसिकं बिस्कं रूप बोलन । गुप्त लिपिया थो रूपय्‌ खुगूगु शदीतक चले जुल । थोयां ल्यू मेगु हिउपाः वःबले थुकी छगू वैशिष्ट्य थो मिलेजुल कि दकों आखलय्‌ कुं (कोण) वा छ्‌यं (शिरोरेखा) समावेश जुल । खुगूगु निसें गुंगूगु शताब्दीया दथुइ हानं अथे हे वैशिष्ट्य बोलन, गुगु थुकी गुप्त लिपिलिसे अलग्ग यानाब्यूगु दु , गथे - (१) गुप्त लिपिया आखःया तपेंगु धोः कोय्‌पाखे खवय्‌ चाःतूगु लूगु दु, व (२) मात्रात बेकोयाः ताहाकः जुयावन । उकिं थुकियात ‘कुटिलाक्षर’ वा ‘कुटिलालिपि’ धयाबिल । गनं गनं ‘विकटाक्षर’ (चाःतूगु लिपि) नं नां दु । मात्रा पूवंगु ई जूगुलिं थुगु ईया लिपियात ‘सिद्धमातृका’ नं धाइ । थो हे लिपिया आधारय्‌ नेपाल लिपिया विकास जुल । व नेपाल लिपिया छगू भेद रञ्जना लिपि बोलन । रञ्जना ज्यान दुगु आखःकथं मान्यता दुगुलिं थुकियात मनूतय्‌ म्हबोनाप जोलाकाः नां छुनातःगु दु ।
american_english: In the course of development of the Brahmi script that emerged in India, Nepal Lipi developed in Nepal with its own distinct style. The chronological period of the Brahmi script is generally considered to be from the 2nd century BCE to the 4th century CE. During this interval, some changes are found to have occurred in these letterforms. From these changes, a new form began to emerge in the 3rd century CE. This was given the name Gupta script, because during the era of the Gupta emperors of India, a form distinct from earlier Brahmi emerged. This form of the Gupta script remained in use until the 6th century. When another change occurred after this, a distinct feature appeared in it whereby an angle (corner) or head (headline) was included in all letters. Between the 6th and 9th centuries, similar distinctive traits emerged again that set it apart from the Gupta script, such as—(1) the straight vertical stroke of the Gupta script letters is found curved to the right at the bottom, and (2) the matras bent and became lengthened. Therefore, it was called 'Kutilakshara' or 'Kutila Lipi'. In some places, it also has the name 'Vikatakshara' (curved script). Because it was an era when the matras were fully formed, the script of this period is also called 'Siddhamatrika'. On the foundation of this very script, Nepal Lipi developed. And the Ranjana script emerged as a variety of Nepal Lipi. Because Ranjana is recognized as a letterform possessing life, it has been named by drawing parallels with human anatomy.

informal_english: In the evolution of the Brahmi script that took off in India, Nepal Lipi developed right in Nepal with its own distinct style. People usually date the Brahmi script from the 2nd century BCE down to the 4th century CE. Over that stretch, you can see some changes creeping into the letterforms. Through these shifts, a brand new form started popping up in the 3rd century CE. They dubbed this the Gupta script, mainly because a form totally different from earlier Brahmi showed up during the reign of India's Gupta emperors. This version of the Gupta script stayed in circulation all the way to the 6th century. When the next wave of change hit, it picked up this neat hallmark where an angle (corner) or head (headline) got worked into every single letter. Between the 6th and 9th centuries, similar telltale features showed up that set it apart from the Gupta script, like—(1) the straight vertical stroke in the Gupta script letters curves off to the right at the bottom, and (2) the matras bent and got stretched out longer. That's why folks called it 'Kutilakshara' or 'Kutila Lipi'. In a few spots, it also goes by the name 'Vikatakshara' (curved script). Since this was the period when matras became fully formed, the script from back then is also called 'Siddhamatrika'. Nepal Lipi developed right off the back of this very script. And the Ranjana script sprang up as a variety of Nepal Lipi. Because people look at Ranjana as a script with a living body, it's actually been named by drawing parallels straight to human anatomy.
